Black Demesne (Z99)

Region in the English ranking survey: Escann.

In one sentence: Win Escann, turn mage privilege into the national constitution, then expand across the world with Acolyte realms and undead armies.

Story: Very high | Mission-tree length: Extremely long (92 Z99-specific mission definitions) | Mission-tree update: current local files supporting EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Uniqueness: Extreme | Waiting and grind: High (formation, Acolyte governance and multiple mission lines) | Early pressure: High for the predecessor; territorial integration remains necessary after formation | Expansion capacity: Extreme.

Not a Starting "Dark Realm"

The ranking table abbreviates the Chinese name, but the current Z99 localisation is 黑暗领域, the Black Demesne. It is not an established country on the 1444 map. This radical vision of magical supremacy requires the player to take another Escanni country through the Wars of Consolidation, choose the appropriate reward and then establish Z99 through a decision. Esthíl is one of the most natural and narratively continuous predecessors, but not the only one: Covenblad, Núrcestir, Wyvernheart and countries with qualifying Witch-King rulers are within the scripted scope. Formation changes Tag and replaces non-generic missions; Esthíl's encyclopedia article, its undead economy, Varina and the War of the Black Tower must not all be counted as parts of the new tree.

The offline English Wiki first presents the Black Demesne as a thought experiment. During the Crimson Deluge, Adelar síl na Whistlehill of the Order of the Iron Sceptre asks why mortal-controlled magic should not replace divine faith when that faith brings war. His manuscripts gain followers during the later Age of Witch-Kings and Esthíl's rise, gradually producing a governing blueprint of the Skull Throne, Acolytes and Apostles. This describes the origins of an ideology, not a state already existing in 1444. The Wiki's writing and character dates are not fixed formation years for every game. Current national ideas instead honour Nichmer as an early ascended Sorcerer-King: the theorist's account and the regime's revered precedent must not be forced into one formation timeline. Compared with the Mages' Peace, the Demesne extends the ambition of magically enforced order across Cannor and even the world.

The Stellar Path: From Victory Reward to Skull Throne

The current formation entrance is "Walk the Stellar Path". The consolidation reward first grants eligible countries can_form_bd; the decision then checks predecessor identity or Witch-King conditions and changes the country to Z99, replacing missions and adopting a special theocratic government and Black Demesne culture. It does not automatically inherit a predecessor's personal story. Coming from Esthíl can feel like Varina's undead country reaching an extreme continuation; coming from another country establishes a different magical empire.

The core change is not merely a flag: it is the creation of the Skull Throne and Acolyte realms. The unique government requires mage or Witch-King rule and allocates power through magical talent and arcane intuition. Newly conquered lands may remain under direct control or be distributed to several Acolytes according to law. Acolytes have influence, land shares and rivalries; the throne can intervene through curses, neglect and favour. Missions add choices over laws, tribute, research and territorial distribution. Wide expansion thus becomes a struggle to divide and control the spoils within a mage empire, rather than direct administration of every province from the capital.

What Will the World Become?

Approximately 92 unique definitions push the front from Escann towards the Alenic north, the Deepwoods, Cannor, Bulwar and World Tree ruins. Early missions reorganise armies, train mage generals and establish the Acolytes. The middle campaign searches for northern magical surges and dragons, contests elven lands and secures forest resources and magical materials. Later, the Nine Pillars, the World Tree's old roots and the Well of Majesty shape an almost deified ruler. These are possible mission futures, not completed starting history. Duels, research and rituals also give the ruler a strong personal roleplaying dimension.

The state claims to select mages by ability rather than bloodline and even criticises slavery; the cost is comprehensive legal oppression of non-casters. The reform text explicitly recognises casters as full citizens while placing ordinary people in a subordinate legal position. Mission "slave liberation" mainly frees potential mages, allowing others to remain in the old system. Another mission conducts involuntary live research on sapient fey of the Deepwoods. The moral issue is not darkness, theocracy or expansion, but institutional control over legal identity, bodies and research consent through magical rank. Even when arriving from Esthíl, its own score of 10 is not simply reused as Z99's result: this card's assessment concerns Z99 itself.

Gameplay and Personality

This extremely long campaign binds conquest, magic and subject governance together. The predecessor must first prevail in Escann. After formation, manage several Acolytes' influence and loyalty, plan who receives land and use undead armies, mage generals and special decisions to take farther regions. More than overwhelming numerical power, the Demesne tests whether you want to maintain this system of mages ruling both mages and ordinary mortals over a long campaign.

v2.1 coordinates: Expansion 96/100 | Authoritarianism 99/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 100/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 100/100) | Pluralism 5/100. v2.1 values: Evil (9/100), trajectory stable. This does not deny the aims of reducing living military service through undead troops or appointing mages regardless of birth. Legal oppression, selective liberation and involuntary experiments outweigh those benefits. The formation decision does not immediately change religion: a later mission, "Breathing Gods", triggers the event that moves the country and its Acolytes to the Black Doctrine. That is a mission future, not every predecessor's starting religion.

Older player guides often recommend approaching through the Iron Sceptre and Esthíl while warning of diplomatic pressure from expansion. A completed-tree campaign report praises the story but describes high micromanagement and time costs. These are 2021–2024 player experiences, not current numerical evidence or a guaranteed optimal route.

Recommended for players who already enjoy Escanni wars, complex subject networks, extreme magic and dark imperial narratives. If you want an egalitarian mage republic, a relaxed short campaign, or no second-class mortals and live experimentation, the Black Demesne is not your country. Original research boundaries remain on the evidence page, with this batch's checks in the English receipt.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as idea groups are filled, and the ambition applies after all seven have been unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Successor ideas do not automatically stack with predecessor ideas. Descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals, not necessarily events completed in 1444. Native English originals are reused, with inherited displayed numbers and unresolved unit qualifications retained.

Black Demesne (Z99) — Black Demesner Ideas

Traditions: Black Demesner Tradition

Effects: shock_damage_received：-20%; Siege ability: +20%.

Idea 1: The Ascendant

In the cosmology of the Black Doctrine, all beings with the capability to use magic are positioned somewhere in a great chain of ascension, sometimes called the 'Ascendant Path'. At the near end of this path are the so-called 'potentiates', people who have latent magical ability but lack the discipline to use it in any consistent and meaningful way. At the far end lies the Universal Mind, the great dispassionate, impersonal intellect which suffuses all the world. The Ascendant is the being who traverses this great path, growing in each stage until they achieve a true union with that purest Intellect. Officially, every Sorcerer-King was Ascendant, though any serious discussion with heretics will reveal that this is a point of much contention.

Effects: Maximum Absolutism: +20.

Idea 2: The Week of Ascension

The Week of Ascension was simultaneously one of the world's most egalitarian institutions and one of its most stratified. Regardless of social class, all non-magical subjects participated in the same festivals and shared in the same activities during the seven-day celebration of virtue. However, every magic user was kept separate from these festivities, instead joining the Sorcerer-King in the Charred Tower for a week of celebration, debauchery, and furious politicking.

Effects: Prestige: +1.

Idea 3: Unrestricted Magic

There have been various attempts to regulate and control magical research throughout the history of the mortal realms. Indeed, perhaps one of the truest signs of a healthy state has been its ability to impose at least some basic restrictions on the activities of mages. In the Black Demesne, to suggest such regulations was not merely seen as foolish, but rather a blasphemous heresy against Doctrine itself. Any law which restricted the development of Intellect was opposed to Doctrine, and restrictions on magic were the most heinous of these.

Effects: All power costs: -5%.

Idea 4: In the Eyes of the Great

Though the non-magical classes could not ascend to the highest rungs of state power in the Demesne, and though they had very limited rights, they nonetheless rose in prominence. Precisely because the most powerful positions were restricted to magic users, these same powerful people often chose to surround themselves with those who could not possibly be a threat. They often promoted members of the non-magical class based on pure competence, justifying the high placement on the basis of intellectual virtue. This was in stark contrast to many other kingdoms, where promotion was by right of blood alone.

Effects: Years of separatism: -5.

Idea 5: The Reaper's Gift

Undead are useful on the field of battle as brute soldiers, but they have very limited capacity to think for themselves or listen to verbal orders. Thus, the Demesne had great need for living scouts, battlefield engineers, and officers. Such positions were an excellent way for non-magical subjects to climb the social ladder by making themselves valuable to mages. Every time war was declared, a great influx of some of the Demesne's most intelligent, driven, and ambitious people came to serve the army in all manner of roles, a pattern that would later earn the moniker of 'the Reaper's Gift'.

Effects: Manpower recovery speed: +15%.

Idea 6: Reformulated Organization

In most societies, mages are typically reclusive academics who have little interest in battlefield glory, and only a smaller portion have the inclination to take up arms and lend their talents to the field of glory. In the Demesne, it was an expectation and personal obligation for every magical initiate to serve for at least some time in the military. This vastly greater pool of magical manpower allowed the Demesne to turn the entire upper officer corps into the exclusive province of mages, allowing decentralized and responsive magical tactics that were far more impressive than any single sorcerer could achieve alone.

Effects: Discipline: +5%; Mages Influence: +10%.

Idea 7: Rings of the Eight

At its greatest extent, the Black Demesne had eight Acolytes, each of whom wore an ebony ring, numbered from the First to the Eighth in order of magical prowess and prominence within the court. The Sorcerer-King wore a matching ring of dark gold, signifying dominance, which would become known as the Ninth ring. Theoretically, as long as one wore the ring of an Acolyte, one was honorbound to give nothing but absolute loyalty to the legitimate bearer of the Ninth ring in all matters. This reminder of hierarchy and control fortified the political order of the Demesne's upper class.

Effects: Governing Capacity Modifier: +10%; Liberty Desire in Subjects on the Same Continent: +1500%.

Ambition: Black Demesner Ambition

Effects: Army morale: +15%.
